text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.8% today to close at $432.74, extending a steep two-week slide of 9.3%. The main driver appears to be a drop in oil prices—crude fell as U.S.-Iran peace talks gained momentum, easing concerns about Middle East supply disruptions that had pushed prices higher earlier in the month. The company also announced a leadership change today, which may have added to selling pressure on a day when the broader refining outlook is already softening.

Refiner profits hinge on the spread between crude costs and fuel prices they can sell. With U.S. oil at $103 and world oil at $123—and refineries running near full capacity at 92.8%—the margin environment is tightening as crude becomes cheaper relative to what it was trading at just days ago. The two-week decline suggests investors are bracing for lower earnings guidance as the oil-price tailwind that lifted the sector earlier in October fades.
